title: 1989 AHSME Problem 10
statement: Consider the sequence defined recursively by \(u_1=a\) (any positive number), and \(u_{n+1}=-\frac{1}{u_n+1},\) \(n=1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots.\) For which of the following values of \(n\) must \(u_n=a?\)

solutions.text:
Direct substitution gives \[ \begin{aligned} u_2&=-\frac1{a+1},\\ u_3&=-\frac{a+1}{a},\\ u_4&=a. \end{aligned} \] The sequence therefore repeats every \(3\) terms, so \(u_n=a\) whenever \(n\equiv1\pmod3.\) Among the choices, only \(16\) has that form.

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Look for the period of the transformation \(x\mapsto-\frac{1}{x+1}\)
